summary: A 120-foot Aermotor fire tower on the Kaibab National Forest, built in 1944 and registered in 1996; current staffing and access not found.

facts.design: Aermotor tower, 120 feet tall, with a groundhouse and support buildings established in 1936

events.note: Current Aermotor tower built, replacing an earlier tower from the 1930s
Groundhouse and support buildings established; NPS record for the Dry Park Lookout Cabin and Storage Sheds gives 1936 as its significant year

evidence.supports: 120-foot tower, tallest fire tower on the Kaibab National Forest
evidence.quote: At 120', Dry Park Lookout is the tallest fire tower on the Kaibab National Forest.
Built in 1944, the Aermotor tower replaced an earlier tower constructed in the 1930s.

evidence.supports: groundhouse and support buildings established 1936; listed on the National Register

notes_for_editor: Construction, height, registration and the 1936 groundhouse listing rest on the NHLR entry, with the NPS record matching the 1936 year. Attributing the NPS cabin-and-sheds record to the same groundhouse is an inference, and the story says so. Current staffing, rental and climbing status were not found: a 2017 Cedar City news item and a Kaibab lookout-rental search surfaced in search but the news page returned HTTP 522 and was not quoted, and the search hits did not establish the status. The 2024 Forest Service cabin-rental results concerned other sites. Brief record checked: elevation 2654.8 m, county, agency and the 1996 registration match, so no corrections were needed. The brief has no built-year event; this record adds 1944 and 1936.
